neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was working as a Junior Engineer with the Delhi Jal Board, was involved in a case where a Constable applied for a water connection in the name of his wife. The accused was alleged to have demanded a bribe of Rs. 1000/- for clearing the file. A trap was laid, and the accused was alleged to have accepted the bribe. The charge-sheet was submitted, and the accused was put on trial. A departmental proceeding was also initiated against the accused, where the enquiry officer found that the evidence did not substantiate the charge of bribe-taking. The disciplinary authority exonerated the accused, but the High Court quashed the criminal proceedings on the premise that the accused had been exonerated in the departmental proceeding. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, stating that the exoneration in the departmental proceeding does not automatically lead to the quashing of the criminal prosecution. The accused was ordered to appear before the trial court for further proceedings.

Supreme Court: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court order, and directed the departmental proceedings to be reopened.

Aggrieved by the same, the State has preferred this special leave petition. Leave granted.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the High Court's order to quash the criminal proceedings was based on an erroneous premise, as the accused had not been exonerated in the departmental proceedings, and that the disciplinary authority's exonerating order was conditional and dependent on the outcome of the criminal case.

quotes.text: The appellant-State intera/ia contended that the assumption of the High Court that the accused had been exonerated in the disciplinary proceedings was unfounded on facts because the report of the enquiry officer was not the final verdict and the same was yet to be considered by the disciplinary authority.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the accused had been exonerated in the departmental proceedings and that the criminal proceedings should be quashed on that ground alone, relying on the precedent set in P.S. Rajya v. State of Bihar.

quotes.text: The accused resorted to another remedy under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and prayed for quashing of the first information report lodged against him under Section 7/13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act. The prayer for quashing of the first information report was founded on the ground that since the accused has been exonerated in the disciplinary proceeding by a detailed speaking order, the first information report deserves to be quashed on that ground alone.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that exoneration in departmental proceedings does not ipso facto lead to the quashing of criminal prosecution, and that the standard of proof in departmental proceedings is lower than that in criminal cases.

quotes.text: Exoneration in the departmental proceeding ipso facto would not lead to quashing of a criminal prosecution.
It is well settled that the standard of proof in departmental proceeding is lower than that of criminal prosecution.
